faDraftCorrectionPack.summary: Narrow follow-up to PR #21: FA/DRAFT 60 rebuilt as a CAP-ordered board (dynasty consensus dropped as a sort input entirely, superseding the 35/50/15 blended methodology described in lastYahooRefresh.resolvedDuringThisRefresh below, which is now historical only). Sort key: CAP dollars descending strictly (CAP column always monotonic, missing=$0) -> Yahoo O-Rank ascending where available -> a small manual-relevance tiebreak (real 2026 draft pick number) for players Yahoo doesn't rank -> name. Candidate universe = every projected cut (all 16 teams) UNION every non-kept Yahoo-ranked player, plus a curated overlay of 16 named 2026 rookies/prospects (force-included if not kept, even if they'd otherwise fall outside the natural top 60) so they are never silently dropped. Implemented in scripts/build_fa_draft_pool.py (candidate generation / metadata enrichment / sort+truncate / render kept as separate, independently-tested functions); regression coverage in tests/test_fa_draft_pool.py.

faDraftCorrectionPack.dynastyOrProxyFix: Owner review: the 5 curated rookies Yahoo does not rank at all (Kingston Flemings, Aday Mara, Ebuka Okorie, Allen Graves, Meleek Thomas) were being mechanically sorted after EVERY real-O-Rank player and ordered only by raw draft-pick number among themselves -- correctly regardless of CAP tier, but wrong within a tier, since some of these rookies have real dynasty value well above some mediocre Yahoo-ranked veterans. Fixed by converting each one's real post-draft dynasty rookie rank (NBC Sports Dynasty Rookie Rankings, 2026 class) into an O-Rank-scale proxy via a through-the-origin least-squares fit calibrated against the curated names that have BOTH a real dynasty rank and a real Yahoo O-Rank (scripts/build_fa_draft_pool.py:_fit_dynasty_or_scale), then using that proxy directly as o_rank so it competes on the same tiebreak axis as real O-Rank -- CAP stays the untouched strict primary key throughout. Net effect: Kingston Flemings (dynasty rank 5) now lands at pool rank 14, ahead of Paul Reed and ~35 other real-O-Rank $0 players, instead of rank 56.
faDraftCorrectionPack.guaranteeScopeFix: Owner review: 'why is there a cluster of rookies at the bottom?' -- the forced-inclusion guarantee had been applied to all 16 curated names, including ones Yahoo DOES rank (Mikel Brown Jr. OR201, Keaton Wagler OR206, Hannes Steinbach OR240), forcing them into the top 60 even though their natural rank (67/71/102 of 185 candidates) was well outside it -- this displaced genuinely better real non-rookie candidates (Aaron Wiggins, De'Anthony Melton, Rui Hachimura) and piled rookies up at the bottom. Fixed: the guarantee now applies ONLY to curated names Yahoo has zero data for at all (Kingston Flemings, Aday Mara, Ebuka Okorie, Allen Graves, Meleek Thomas -- exactly the ones the dynasty-OR-proxy above covers) plus Paul Reed unconditionally. A curated name Yahoo does rank, even weakly, now competes purely on merit and can legitimately miss the cut -- Brown/Wagler/Steinbach no longer force-included; Boozer/Wilson/Dybantsa/Peterson/Acuff/Lendeborg/Morez Johnson/Burries still clear the pool naturally on real merit, unaffected. See scripts/build_fa_draft_pool.py: Candidate.guaranteed, set at construction time from which data path actually supplied each candidate (Yahoo vs. dynasty-proxy-backed overlay), not from a static name list.
faDraftCorrectionPack.srcBadgeFix: Owner-spotted bug: rookies found via the live Yahoo fetch (e.g. Cameron Boozer, AJ Dybantsa) were showing the 'FA' SRC badge instead of 'R', because the badge was keyed off which data path supplied the candidate rather than the independent rookie flag. Fixed in scripts/build_fa_draft_pool.py:src_badge_html -- badge priority is now cut (team short name) > rookie ('R') > 'FA', so every rookie shows 'R' regardless of source, and a cut player who happens to also be a curated rookie (not currently the case in this league) still correctly shows the cut team's name.

All 16 teams' kept-player rows are now sorted by cap dollars descending (owner directive, applied board-wide).

Fixed a parsing bug from the first refresh pass: 5 cut-chips carrying a pre-existing '$N' cap annotation (e.g. Julius Randle, Alperen Şengün) were being silently dropped by the cut-list regex. Re-parsed from the true pre-refresh index.html and now every nonzero-live-cap cut chip across all 16 teams carries a refreshed annotation (owner directive: 'for cuts you gotta remember to keep the cap numbers').

Fixed the FA/Draft-60 pool sort, in several owner-reviewed rounds. The board's meta-strip label ('35% DYNASTY / 50% YAHOO / 15% CAP') describes a real documented rule found in local_sources/nba_talk_vn_dynasty_forensic_state_2026-08-20.md (non-canonical for data, but the source of this process note): 'salary descending first; within a salary tier, current consensus/ADP/current fantasy utility, with dynasty upside used when consensus thins out... established NOW players can and should sit above speculative rookies.' FINAL state: cap dollars descending is the strict primary key (owner: 'sort fa pool by cap number' -- CAP column is always monotonically non-increasing); within an exact cap tie, a 0.50/0.35-weighted blend of live Yahoo oRank and Hashtag Basketball's live crowdsourced dynasty ranking (hashtagbasketball.com/fantasy-basketball-dynasty-rankings, 400 players, updated 2026-09-14) decides order (owner: 'sort a mix of yahoo and dynasty'), with a neutral oRank=150 substituted for anyone outside Yahoo's 300-fetch so that absence doesn't unfairly bury a dynasty-good player.

Fixed a coverage gap: the pool universe was built only from Yahoo's 300-player fetch, so ~105 current players (mostly 2026 rookies + deep bench, e.g. Kingston Flemings, Allen Graves, Nate Ament, Aday Mara) that fell outside Yahoo's window were invisible to the pool regardless of dynasty rank (owner: 'missing a lot of rookies'). Backfilled them from the same Hashtag dynasty page (name + position + NBA team from its own badges, $0 cap, since no live cap data exists for them), translating its team abbreviations to Yahoo's convention (GS->GSW, NO->NOP, NY->NYK, PHO->PHX, SA->SAS). Added a hard dedup guard after two near-miss duplicates surfaced during testing (Bub Carrington / Carlton Carrington and Jimmy Butler / Jimmy Butler III are the same people under different name spellings on the two sources).

Fixed the rookie ('R') classification. It had inherited the pre-refresh board's rookie tags as-is, which mixed in players who were actually 2025 draftees now in their second year (owner: 'rookies in 2026 not 2025 ok'). Fetched the real, complete 2026 NBA draft class (all 60 picks, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_draft) and made it the single source of truth for the rookie flag and purple rookie-row styling, overriding whatever the old board said. Net effect combined with the coverage-gap fix: 21 verified rookies now surface in the top 60 (was 15, some of them wrongly tagged).

Fixed two more bugs surfaced by owner review: (1) a health-badge extraction regex never captured the badge's title tooltip text, so every kept/cut player's INJ/REC badge lost its title (e.g. 'Meniscus rehab') and 2 cut-list badges (Moses Moody, Donte DiVincenzo) were dropped entirely during the first pool rebuild -- re-parsed from the true pre-refresh index.html and restored all 9 original badges with correct titles. (2) Jonathan Kuminga (DHA) was still showing NBA team ATL, a stale value carried through untouched because he's outside Yahoo's 300-player fetch; both the prior Yahoo snapshot and the live Hashtag dynasty page agree he's on MIN, so kept players missing from the live Yahoo fetch now also fall back to the dynasty page's team/position data instead of staying on stale board values.

yahooRefreshAutomation.summary: Fixed: the merged .github/workflows/yahoo-refresh.yml (PR #20) only ever wrote an ephemeral artifact -- it had no contents:write/pull-requests:write permissions and no git-commit/gh-pr-create step at all. Confirmed by diffing PR #20's merged headRefOid against the stale local/remote branch ci/yahoo-refresh-workflow: the PR-creation commit (13aac3c, 'replace ephemeral artifact handoff with Yahoo data PR') was pushed to that branch AFTER PR #20 already merged, so it was never part of main -- this explains Run #3 (CHANGED, old 130/175 -> new 130/176) producing no PR despite a green run.
yahooRefreshAutomation.fix: Added permissions (contents/pull-requests: write) and one new workflow step, 'Promote CHANGED refresh to a single candidate PR', calling the new top-level promote-yahoo-refresh.sh. On CHANGED it mechanically regenerates index.html (scripts/refresh_keeper_board_display.py for kept-player Yahoo-sourced pos/nba/cap display -- never roster membership -- then scripts/build_fa_draft_pool.py for the FA/DRAFT 60), runs the full test suite + ./validate.sh as a hard gate, stages data/yahoo/ + index.html on branch automation/yahoo-refresh, and opens/updates exactly ONE PR (scripts/prepare_yahoo_data_pr.py builds its title/body). Asserts the PR actually exists afterward -- CHANGED with no PR is a non-zero exit, never a silent/green no-op. On MATCH, no PR is touched. This is the single-PR model requested -- no second issue/PR step, unlike the never-merged ci/yahoo-refresh-workflow branch's design.
yahooRefreshAutomation.relatedFix: refresh-yahoo.sh's MATCH/CHANGED comparison was hardcoding PUBLISHED_FLOOR/CEILING = 130, 175 -- stale since PR #21/#22 promoted the canonical floor/ceiling to 131/177 (see canonicalState.capFloor/capCeiling above). Left unfixed, every future refresh would report CHANGED forever regardless of real Yahoo movement. Now reads ai_exchange/CURRENT_STATE.json's canonicalState.capFloor/capCeiling, falling back to the old hardcoded pair only if that file/keys are unavailable.
yahooRefreshAutomation.knownLimitation: GITHUB_TOKEN-authored pushes/PRs do not auto-trigger this repo's own push/pull_request-triggered CI (validate.yml, claude-code-review.yml) -- a documented GitHub Actions anti-recursion behavior, not a bug in this fix. The PR body says so and recommends manually re-running checks on the opened PR. Confirmed repository setting (gh api .../actions/permissions/workflow): can_approve_pull_request_reviews=true, i.e. 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests' is already enabled, so PR creation itself is not blocked.
yahooRefreshAutomation.testCoverage: tests/test_promote_yahoo_refresh.py (end-to-end via a throwaway git repo + fake gh, no live network/auth), tests/test_refresh_keeper_board_display.py, tests/test_prepare_yahoo_data_pr.py, tests/test_refresh_yahoo_published_baseline.py, and new cases in tests/test_yahoo_refresh_workflow.py.
